item.text: {"winner":"A","confidence":"high","summary":"A is closer to the frozen contract because it adds the replayable Upload API while preserving FilesService.Add. B makes an explicitly forbidden behavioral change to Add by buffering every caller-provided multipart body.","reasons":["A uses multipartbody.NewFile with field \"file\", validates filename/content, and produces a replayable upload body.","A leaves the existing lower-level Add API unchanged; B adds io.ReadAll and changes Add's memory use, reader-error semantics, cancellation behavior, and retry behavior.","Neither candidate actually routes Upload through the existing public Add method. A duplicates Add's request/response logic, while B extracts a private add helper and bypasses Add. A's defect is more localized and easier to correct.","B has the stronger retry test because it uses an actual os.File and verifies multipart contents on both attempts. A only counts attempts and does not explicitly set RetryAllMethods: true, matching the report less precisely."],"risks_a":["Upload duplicates Add's option, request, decoding, and missing-data logic, creating maintenance drift and violating the required reuse path.","Tests omit required empty-filename, nil-content, and source-reader-error coverage.","The retry test does not inspect the body on the retried request."],"risks_b":["Buffering all Add bodies violates the requirement to preserve Add behavior and may impose unbounded memory use or block reading before request context handling begins.","Upload does not call FilesService.Add as explicitly required.","The new Add retry test codifies behavior outside the requested scope and contrary to the frozen contract; validation and source-reader-error tests are still missing."]}
